title: Criticality-Aware Instruction-Centric Bandwidth Partitioning for Data Center Applications
problem: Co-locating latency-critical (LC) and best-effort (BE) tasks on shared datacenter nodes causes memory bandwidth contention that results in priority inversion, where BE tasks monopolize bandwidth and cause LC tasks to violate quality-of-service (QoS) requirements.
motivation: Improving datacenter utilization through workload co-location is economically essential, but existing bandwidth partitioning schemes either fail to enforce LC QoS or waste bandwidth by over-protecting all LC memory accesses indiscriminately.
method: Pivot is a bandwidth partitioning system that prioritizes LC memory accesses at every component along the full memory path (L1/L2/L3 caches, DRAM controller) rather than at a single bottleneck point. Critically, Pivot selectively prioritizes only performance-critical loads—those causing long stalls on the re-order buffer (ROB)—rather than all LC accesses. A two-phase profiling technique identifies these critical loads offline with minimal runtime overhead: Phase 1 profiles whole-execution hit/miss behavior per load PC, and Phase 2 uses those profiles to tag critical loads for hardware prioritization during production runs.
key_novelty: Instruction-centric identification of ROB-stalling critical loads combined with full-memory-path prioritization, avoiding bandwidth waste from protecting non-critical LC accesses.
contributions: Two-phase profile-guided technique to identify performance-critical loads (ROB-stalling) with minimal overhead
Full memory path prioritization of critical LC loads across all cache levels and DRAM controller
Up to 34.5% improvement in effective machine utilization vs. state-of-the-art approaches
Up to 2.76x higher BE throughput while maintaining LC QoS guarantees

metrics.other: Up to 34.5% effective machine utilization improvement; up to 2.76x BE throughput improvement vs. state-of-the-art

limitations: Relies on offline profiling to identify critical loads, which may not generalize well to dynamically varying workload phases or previously unseen applications.
primary_theme: Criticality-aware instruction-level memory bandwidth partitioning for LC/BE co-location
